events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 920 AM PDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Whittier, moving north at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Frequent lightning and Pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor hail damage to vegetation is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Long Beach...
Downtown Los Angeles...
Pasadena...
Torrance...
Inglewood...
Carson...
Redondo Beach...
Glendale...
Baldwin Park...
Boyle Heights...
Santa Fe Springs...
and Highland Park.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Inner waters from Point Mugu to San Mateo Pt. CA including Santa Catalina and Anacapa Islands; Outer waters from Santa Cruz Island to San Clemente Island to 60 NM offshore including San Nicolas and Santa Barbara Islands
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Tropical moisture will continue to stream over the area and bring
a slight chance of thunderstorms to the coastal waters through
this afternoon, with storms developing over the southern coastal
waters this morning, moving to the northeast. Any thunderstorm
that forms will be capable of producing locally gale force winds
and rough seas, dangerous lightning, and brief heavy rainfall with
reduced visibility.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to 1 AM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (6.99 ft MLLW) at 9:59 PM
Tuesday 9/8 and 1.0 ft above normal (6.79 ft MLLW) at 10:54 PM
Wednesday 9/9. These predictions include up to 0.6 ft of storm
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later
along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Hardin, TX; Jefferson, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Hardin,
Jasper, Orange and Jefferson Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 26.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:45 AM CDT Tuesday was 27.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 19.4 feet Sunday
morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 26.7
feet on 04/24/1977.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Dawson/McCone/Prairie/Richland/Wibaux Counties
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The National Weather Service in Glasgow has issued a Fire Weather
Watch, which is in effect from Thursday afternoon through
Thursday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zone 122.

* WIND...WEST AT 10 TO 20 WITH GUSTS TO 30 MPH.

* HUMIDITY...AS LOW AS 11 PERCENT.

* THUNDERSTORMS...NONE.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will possibly spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
